events.title: Execution of Mary, Queen of Scots
events.description: Mary, Queen of Scots, was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle in England after being implicated in the Babington Plot to assassinate her cousin, Queen Elizabeth I.
events.significance: Her death removed a central Catholic claimant to the English throne and heightened tensions with Catholic Spain, contributing to the launch of the Spanish Armada in 1588. Her son James VI of Scotland later succeeded Elizabeth as James I of England.

events.title: Birth of Jules Verne
events.description: Jules Verne, the French novelist, was born in Nantes, France. He went on to write adventure novels such as Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, Journey to the Center of the Earth, and Around the World in Eighty Days.
events.significance: Verne is regarded as a founding father of science fiction. His works anticipated technologies such as submarines and space travel and remain among the most translated books in the world.

events.title: Japan Attacks Port Arthur, Beginning the Russo-Japanese War
events.description: Japanese forces launched a surprise torpedo boat attack on the Russian fleet at Port Arthur, Manchuria, starting the Russo-Japanese War before a formal declaration of war.
events.significance: Japan's victory in the war in 1905 marked the first major defeat of a European power by an Asian nation in the modern era, established Japan as a rising world power, and contributed to the unrest that led to the 1905 Russian Revolution.

events.title: Incorporation of the Boy Scouts of America
events.description: The Boy Scouts of America was incorporated by William D. Boyce, inspired by the scouting movement founded in Britain by Robert Baden-Powell.
events.significance: The organization grew into one of the largest youth movements in the United States, shaping youth education, outdoor activity, and civic engagement for generations.

events.title: NASDAQ Stock Market Begins Trading
events.description: The National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations system, NASDAQ, began trading as the world's first electronic stock market.
events.significance: NASDAQ pioneered electronic trading and later became home to many major technology companies, transforming global financial markets.
